newsitem.title: UK: HK's Patten say no progress on ethnic minorities.
newsitem.headline: HK's Patten say no progress on ethnic minorities.

text.p: Hong Kong governor Chris Patten said on Monday that he could not "say hand on heart that we have made any progress" on enhancing the rights of the colony's ethnic minorities to settle in Britain.
Speaking to reporters at the Confederation of British Industry's annual conference here, Patten said there had been no change in the British government's position since the spring.
"I last discussed the issue with the Home Secretary Michael Howard a couple of weeks ago,but I didn't get a new or different line on that occasion," he said.

The comments come on the heels of press reports that Patten and Queen Elizabeth had both applied pressure to the government to grant British residency rights to a number of Hong Kong minorities when China takes control in July 1997.

The Guardian newspaper reported on Monday that up to 3,500 people from Indian and other minorities whose British citizenship was reclassifed to remove their right of abode in Britain would effectively become stateless after the handover.
Patten said he expected the issue to be raised in the House of Commons on Thursday, when parliament holds its last formal debate on the territory.
